info.name: SupportDesk API
info.description:
Real-time customer support and ticketing system (Express + MongoDB, Socket.IO).

HOW TO RUN
1. Pick the server with `baseUrl` and `serverUrl` (local by default; the production values are listed under the variable descriptions).
2. Set `adminEmail` and `adminPassword` to the seeded admin account. Never commit real passwords.
3. Run the folders in order: 0 Setup, 1 Auth, 2 Admin - Users, then 3 to 7. Tokens and ids are stored in collection variables by the test scripts.
4. Folder 7 closes the ticket for good, so it is last. To run the flow again, run 3 > 'Create ticket' first to get a fresh ticket.

Every response is `{ success, data }` on success and `{ success: false, message }` on error.
Protected requests send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

variable.description: Same host without /api, used for Socket.IO. Production: https://customer-support-system-api-1qcu.onrender.com
Fill in locally. Do not commit it.

item.name: 0. Setup
item.description: Health check and the Socket.IO handshake probe. No login needed.

request.description: Proves the Socket.IO server is reachable. A healthy server answers 200 with a session id and `upgrades: ["websocket"]`. This only checks the handshake endpoint; real events need a Socket.IO client (see the 'Real-time' folder description).

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description:
Register and log in the three test accounts. Each login stores the token and the user id in collection variables, and every other folder reads them from there.

The admin account comes from the seed script (`npm run seed:admin`); set `adminEmail` and `adminPassword` in the collection variables first. Register always creates a CUSTOMER, so the agent is registered here and promoted in folder 2.

Rate limits: login allows 10 failed attempts per 15 minutes per IP, register allows 20 per hour.

request.description: Returns 409 if the email already exists. That is fine on a second run; just log in.

exec: pm.test("Created (201) or already registered (409)", function () { pm.expect([201, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Registration cannot choose a role. This account becomes an AGENT in folder 2 (Change role).

exec: pm.test("Created (201) or already registered (409)", function () { pm.expect([201, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Tokens are stateless, so this does not invalidate the token; the client just discards it.

item.name: 2. Admin - Users
item.description: Admin only. Promote the registered agent account to AGENT.

request.description: This is the list the web app uses for the assign dropdown.

item.name: Change role: agent account to AGENT

request.description: Run this once after registering the agent. Rules: an admin cannot change their own role (400), and an agent with open tickets cannot be demoted (409). Changing a role also closes that user's open sockets, so they reconnect with the new role.

item.name: 3. Tickets - Customer
item.description: A customer only ever sees their own tickets. Tickets outside the caller's scope answer 404, so their existence is not revealed.

request.description: Priority, status and assignee sent in the body are ignored. New tickets are OPEN with MEDIUM priority.

query.description: OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_FOR_CUSTOMER, RESOLVED or CLOSED
GENERAL, BILLING, TECHNICAL, ACCOUNT or OTHER
An agent id, or the word unassigned

request.description: Tick the disabled query parameters to filter, search, sort and paginate.
The response includes allowedNextStatuses for the caller's role.
Customers can change subject, description and category while the ticket is OPEN. Changing the priority returns 403.

item.name: 4. Tickets - Admin
item.description: Admins see every ticket and assign them to agents. Assign before the agent starts work: a ticket needs an assignee before it can move to IN_PROGRESS.

query.description: OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_FOR_CUSTOMER, RESOLVED or CLOSED
GENERAL, BILLING, TECHNICAL, ACCOUNT or OTHER
An agent id, or the word unassigned

request.description: Only users with the AGENT role can be assigned. Reassigning is allowed and takes the previous agent out of the ticket's real-time room. Writes a system line into the conversation and emits ticket_assigned.

item.name: Assign to the same agent again (400)

request.description: Emits ticket_updated with the fields that really changed.

item.name: Customer cannot use the admin list (403)
5. Tickets - Agent
item.description: An agent only sees the tickets assigned to them. Promote the agent in folder 2 and assign the ticket in folder 4 first.

query.description: OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_FOR_CUSTOMER, RESOLVED or CLOSED
GENERAL, BILLING, TECHNICAL, ACCOUNT or OTHER
An agent id, or the word unassigned

request.description: Emits ticket_status_changed and writes a system line into the conversation.
Agents may only change the priority of their assigned tickets.
Sets resolvedAt. The customer then confirms with CLOSED, or an agent reopens it with IN_PROGRESS.
RESOLVED cannot go to WAITING_FOR_CUSTOMER.
The transition exists, but only the customer or an admin may perform it.

item.name: 6. Conversation (messages)
item.description:
Threaded replies on a ticket. The customer, the assigned agent and admins can read and write; everyone else gets 404. Messages are 1 to 2000 characters, and nothing can be sent to a CLOSED ticket.

Messages are sent over REST only. After a message is saved, the server broadcasts a ticket_message event to everyone in the ticket room, and the sender also gets the message in this response, so clients match messages by `_id`.

Edit rules: only the sender can edit, only TEXT messages, only within 15 minutes of sending (see `editableUntil`), and not on a closed ticket. Not even an admin can edit someone else's message. There is no delete.

Rate limit: sending or editing messages is limited to 20 per minute per user; after that the API answers 429 until the minute is over.

query.description: Older messages than this message id (load earlier)
Only messages newer than this id (catch up after a reconnect). Use either before or after, not both.

request.description: Returns data.messages (oldest first) and hasMore. System lines (assignments, status changes) are part of the conversation.

exec: pm.test("Has messages and hasMore", function () { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j.data.messages).to.be.an("array"); pm.expect(j).to.have.property("hasMore"); });

item.name: List messages older than the agent reply
List messages newer than the first one (reconnect catch-up)

request.description: Sets editedAt and broadcasts the updated message to the room. Sending the same text again changes nothing.

item.name: Agent cannot edit the customer's message (403)
Admin cannot edit the customer's message (403)
7. Notifications
item.description:
Run after the conversation folder so there is something to read. Everyone only ever sees their own notifications. NEW_REPLY notifications are grouped: one unread entry per ticket with a `count`. A notification is deleted automatically 90 days after its last event.

Types: TICKET_CREATED, TICKET_ASSIGNED, STATUS_CHANGED, NEW_REPLY, SLA_AT_RISK, SLA_BREACHED.

exec: pm.test("Has items and an unread count", function () { pm.expect(body.data).to.be.an("array"); pm.expect(body.unreadCount).to.be.a("number"); });

item.name: Mark all read for one ticket
Someone else's notification is not found (404)
8. Admin - Analytics
item.description: Admin only. Figures describe tickets created in the range (default: last 30 days, at most 366 days). The `current` figures (overdue, at risk, unassigned, open now) are right now, across all dates. `tz` may be any IANA name in any letter case; days and weeks are cut in it.

item.name: 9. Finish
item.description: Closing a ticket is final, so these run last.

item.name: Customer confirms and closes the ticket

request.description: RESOLVED to CLOSED is the customer confirming the fix. From OPEN the same request is a cancel.

item.name: Closed ticket accepts no new messages (400)
10. Real-time (Socket.IO)
item.description:
Postman cannot import Socket.IO requests, so use a Socket.IO client (Postman's own Socket.IO request type, or the browser/Node client) against `{{serverUrl}}`.

CONNECT: send the JWT in the handshake auth object, not in the URL: `{ "auth": { "token": "<customerToken>" } }`. A missing, invalid or expired token is rejected with the error `Not authenticated`.

CLIENT EVENTS (with an acknowledgement callback):
- `join_ticket` with `{ "ticketId": "<id>" }`. The ack is `{ ok: true, participants: [...] }`, or `{ ok: false, message }`. Only the ticket's customer, its assigned agent and admins can join; everyone else gets `Ticket not found`.
- `leave_ticket` with `{ "ticketId": "<id>" }`.

SERVER EVENTS:
- `ticket_message` `{ ticketId, message }`: a new message, a system line, or an edited message (same `_id`, so replace it instead of adding it). Sent only after the message is saved.
- `ticket_updated` `{ ticketId, changedFields, updatedBy }`.
- `ticket_status_changed` `{ ticketId, ticketNumber, from, to, resolvedAt, changedBy }`.
- `ticket_assigned` `{ ticketId, ticketNumber, subject, assignedTo, previousAssignee, assignedBy }`. Also delivered to the new and the previous agent without joining the ticket room.
- `user_joined` / `user_left` `{ ticketId, user: { id, name, role } }`. One person with several tabs counts once.

Payloads are the same for everyone in the room, so they only say what changed; fetch the ticket again for role specific data such as allowedNextStatuses.

To watch it live: connect two clients (customer and agent), join the same ticket on both, then run the 'Send message' requests in folder 6.

NOTIFICATION EVENTS (delivered to your own user room automatically, no join needed): `notification` `{ notification, unreadCount }` for a new or updated (grouped) notification, and `notifications_updated` `{ unreadCount }` when notifications were marked read or removed.
